primary_claim: Matryoshka SAEs, trained with a sum of SAE losses computed on random prefixes of the latents, completely avoid the feature-absorption holes seen in vanilla SAEs on a toy model, and when trained on a 4-layer TinyStories language model achieve higher Mean Max Correlation with small reference-SAE features than vanilla SAEs at the same L0 (across most model locations), at the cost of a slightly worse Fraction of Variance Unexplained.

effect.metric: Mean Max Correlation (MMC) with reference SAE latents; Fraction of Variance Unexplained (FVU)
effect.value: Matryoshka SAEs have higher MMC than vanilla SAEs at the same L0 across most locations (exceptions: residual stream before first block, first attention-layer output); at fixed L0, Matryoshka has slightly worse FVU, comparable to a vanilla SAE ~0.4x its size

contradicts_or_qualifies: Addresses feature absorption and fragmentation problems identified in vanilla SAEs by Chanin et al. (2024, arXiv:2409.14507)
stated_future_work: Validate these results with more 'real' language models and train SAEs with much more data
Understand why Matryoshka sometimes has less-interpretable lower activations than vanilla SAEs
Understand why matryoshka parent latents have larger activations when their children features are active
Explore whether another distribution (besides the truncated Pareto) works better for prefix-length sampling, or choose it dynamically during training
Test whether Matryoshka SAEs work well with newer architectures like JumpReLU and Crosscoder SAEs
limitations_stated: SAEs were only trained for 100M tokens (1/3 of the TinyStories dataset); the language model itself was trained for only 3 epochs on the 300M-token TinyStories dataset
Matryoshka sometimes has less-interpretable lower activations than vanilla SAEs
At a fixed L0, Matryoshka SAEs have slightly worse Fraction of Variance Unexplained than vanilla SAEs
The Pareto distribution used for prefix-length sampling was selected without much optimization
Reconstruction loss at a fixed L0 may not be the right metric if true features form a DAG
quote: My results demonstrate that Matryoshka SAEs reduce feature absorption while preserving abstract features.
